profile.name: Pawan Shrestha
profile.headline: Computer engineer. I build models and software that measure the real world.
profile.shortBio: Recent Computer Engineering graduate with a strong foundation in full-stack web development, machine learning, and AI systems.
profile.bio: I'm Pawan Shrestha, a Computer Engineering graduate from Nepal Engineering College. I spent my final year training a U-Net on satellite imagery to forecast urban sprawl across Kathmandu, Pokhara, and Hyderabad, it hit 85% accuracy on land-classification. I also build practical web apps end to end: a complaint-reporting platform for city maintenance and a music-sharing social app. I write Python, and I care about models that hold up outside a Jupyter notebook: real data pipelines, real APIs, real deployments. I'm looking for a junior role in software engineering, ML, or data science where I can do that work for a product with users.
profile.availability: Open to junior software, AI, and data science opportunities

projects.title: Urban Sprawl Prediction
projects.summary: A U-Net that forecasts where Kathmandu, Lalitpur, and Bhaktapur will grow by 2030.
projects.description: Trained a U-Net on Landsat satellite imagery to classify built-up vs non-built-up land, reaching 85% accuracy across the three cities. I chained it into a ConvLSTM that extends those classifications forward, so the model outputs 2030 sprawl maps at 78% precision. The pipeline — image tiling, augmentation, training, and map rendering — is all pandas, scikit-learn, and TensorFlow, and I wrote the visualizations that turn predictions into readable growth maps.

projects.title: AI Agent with RAG & Tool-Calling
projects.summary: A Python AI agent built with LangChain. It answers questions from general knowledge, from your own local documents (RAG), from live web search, or with a calculator
projects.description: An LLM-powered conversational agent that combines Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with dynamic tool-calling and memory. Built using LangChain and the Gemini API, it ingests custom documents into local vector databases (Chroma) for grounded context and executes live web searches for real-time query routing, all accessible via an interactive Streamlit UI.

projects.title: CleanCity
projects.summary: A civic reporting platform where a photo and GPS pin log a city issue for officials to resolve.
projects.description: Residents upload a photo of a problem — garbage, a pothole, a blocked drain — with their location. I built the classification step with an AI model that identifies the issue type so it routes to the right department, then an admin dashboard where officials track and close each complaint. It runs on Next.js with a Supabase backend and OpenStreetMap for geolocation.

projects.title: Near Beat
projects.summary: A full-stack web application that helps people discover, join, and chat about nearby real-world events in real time.
projects.description: NearBeat is a full-stack event discovery platform that connects users with nearby local activities. It features location-based event search, real-time participant chat, instant notifications, and secure user authentication built on a robust React, Node.js, and PostgreSQL stack.

projects.title: Melomatch
projects.summary: A social app where strangers post a song and discover what others are listening to.
projects.description: Users create profiles, post the song they can't stop replaying, and browse strangers' picks. I built the REST API in Node/Express with MongoDB for profiles and posts, and the React frontend handles auth, feed pagination, and a like system. The interesting part was designing the data model so a post can surface three different feed orders — recent, liked, and from people with overlapping taste.
